items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: So, I was with Fletcher in '35 and while I was with Fletcher, Cab sent me

ctx.x: Yeah, I went back with Fletcher in '35 and we went on -- in the latter part of '34 and in '35 we went to Chicago to play in a cabaret out there. I found out that musicians in Chicago -- there were quite a few of them stranded. They wanted to put them out of hotels because of their deportment and musicians would then -- the dignity -- they'd lost all of it. As the younger ones came in -- the older ones knew how to deport themselves, but the younger ones came in and the dignity wasn't part of their profession at…

Fletcher owed me money, so I just quit without notice -- I gave him notice (unintelligible) Cab offered me $125.00 a week and with Fletcher most of the time on the road I got nothing. So, since Fletcher was a personal friend of mine, he'd been with me for many years -- as a matter of fact, he lived in my house when he came to New York.
